title: Single step of the carry phase
statement: Let $x$ be a finite binary input word, let $p$ be a valid input-head position for $x$, and let $a,b$ be finite binary words. Starting in state $1$ with input-head position $p$, work-head position $|a|$, the tape containing the concatenation of $a$ and $b$, and empty output, one step of the four-state binary-counter machine has the following effect: if $b$ begins with $1$, it enters state $1$, moves the work head right by one, and changes the tape word to $a$ followed by $0$ and the tail of $b$; otherwise it enters state $2$, moves the work head left by one, and changes the tape word to $a$ followed by $1$ and the tail of $b$. The input-head position remains $p$ and the output remains empty.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is a finite binary input word
$p$ is a valid input-head position for $x$
replaced:
Suppose the four-state binary-counter machine is in its carry state with the
concatenation of binary words $p$ and $b$ on the nonnegative work-tape cells,
work head at cell $|p|$, and empty output. If $b$ begins with $1$, one step
clears that bit to $0$ and moves the work head right, staying in the carry
state; otherwise one step writes $1$ at cell $|p|$ (replacing the first bit of
$b$, or extending the word) and moves the work head left, entering the rewind
state. The input head does not move.
